ACUTE CORONARY SYNDROME ALGORITHM 
 
 
Risk Factors for ACS 
* Age ≥ 65 years 
* Smoker 
* Family history of CAD 
* Diabetes Mellitus 
* Hypercholestrolaemia 
* Hypertension 
* Drug Abuse: cocaine,  
   metamphetamine 
* Previous MI 
* HIV ± HAART (PI) 
Patient presenting with chest pain or symptoms 
suggestive of ischaemia or infarction 
TRIAGE - ORANGE 
Immediate Assessment 
* ABCs 
* General appearance 
* Focused physical examination 
* 12 & 15 lead ECG (V4R, V7-9) 
* Check vital signs, O2 sats 
* Establish IV access  
* Finger prick glucose 
* Bloods : Troponin I/SOB panel; U+E; FBC; VBG 
* Detailed history 
* Portable CXR 
Immediate General Treatment 
* Support ABCs 
* If O2 Sats < 94% start nasal prong O2 @  
   2L/min, titrate 
* Aspirin 300 mg chewed stat 
* Nitroglycerin (1st check ECG, see box for contraindications) 
   Nitrolingual Spray®: 1 spray at 5 minute     
   intervals (max 3 sprays in 15min)  
   Sublingual: 1 tablet repeated for total 3  
   doses at 5 min intervals 
* Morphine IV if discomfort not relieved by  
   nitroglycerin: 1-2mg alloquots  
Contraindications 
Aspirin 
* Known hypersensitivity to  
   aspirin - Give patient  
   Clopidogrel 300mg stat po 
 
Relative Contraindications 
* Active peptic ulcer disease 
* Bleeding disorder 
* Allergy 
Contraindications 
Nitroglycerine 
* Hypotension SBP < 90mmHg  
* Severe bradycardia < 50 bpm 
* Severe tachycardia > 100 bpm 
* RV infarction (associated with   
   inferior MI) 
* Use of phosphodiesterase  
   inhibitors eg Sildenafil (Viagra®) /      
   Vardenafil (Levitra®) within 24hrs;  
   Tadalafil (Cialis®) within 48hrs. 
12 , 15 lead & V4R 
ECG interpretation 
STEMI 
* ST Elevation in 2 or more contiguous leads  
   (see box for criteria) 
* New LBBB or presumably  
   new LBBB (Sgarbossa's criteria) 
* True posterior MI: tall R in V1 & STE ≥ 0.5mm   
   in V7-9  
* RV infarction: ST elevation V4R  
NSTE - ACS 
High Risk Unstable Angina (UA) / NSTEMI 
* ST depression ≥ 0.5mm (see box for criteria) 
* ST elevation > 0.5mm but < 1mm 
* Dynamic inverted t-waves                                                   
  i.e. T-waves previously been upright but are inverted  
  when the patient has chest pain 
Intermediate/ Low Risk UA 
Normal or non-diagnostic 
  changes in ST segment or t-waves 
* ST deviation < 0.5mm  
* T-wave inversion ≤ 2mm  
Contiguous Leads 
* Inferior:  II, III, aVF 
* Lateral: I, aVL, V5, V6 
* Anterior: V3, V4 
* Septal: V1, V2 
Dr R Gihwala CMJAH Emergency Department June 2020 
Refer to respective protocol for 
further management
